fact: Botswana's Minister of Communications and Innovation and Namibia's Minister of ICT signed an ICT cooperation MoU in Kasane on 7 August 2026, covering digital transformation, cybersecurity, ICT infrastructure, connectivity, innovation, skills and emerging technologies.

Botswana's Ministry of Communications and Innovation says Namibia was among the first countries in the region to significantly reduce roaming charges with Botswana; the article gives no date for the cut, so the published date is used.
BOCRA announced that Botswana takes part with Malawi, Lesotho, Mozambique, Zambia and Zimbabwe in the SADC One Network Area framework to harmonise mobile roaming tariffs.

Operators including Orange Botswana, Mascom Wireless and BTC have implemented the new One Network Area roaming tariffs, with cuts of 10% to 98.6% and free incoming SMS across participating countries; Botswana-Zambia data roaming fell by up to 94%.
Reduced roaming rates between Botswana and Namibia took effect in August 2024.

Botswana was among the delegates (with South Africa, Comoros and Eswatini) at the SADC Regional Workshop on Data Governance in Harare on data policy harmonisation; the article gives no event date, so the published date is used.

Botswana sent a delegation, led by its Ambassador to Zimbabwe, to the second African Preparatory Meeting (APM26-2) convened by the African Telecommunications Union in Victoria Falls on 27-29 May 2026, which drew 35 ATU member states, and took part in the discussions on common African positions.
